product: Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit territories and AK112 elsewhere, is an investigational tetravalent PD-1 and VEGF bispecific antibody engineered by Akeso. Summit holds exclusive rights in North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Japan; it is approved only in China, not by any regulator in Summit's territories.
demand: Unmet need is large across EGFR-mutated NSCLC after third-generation TKI failure, first-line PD-L1-positive NSCLC, biliary tract cancer, colorectal cancer and bladder cancer. Akeso reports over 70,000 patients treated commercially in China and over 4,000 in trials, evidence of real underlying demand, but approved-territory demand is entirely unproven until the 2026-11-14 FDA decision.
pricing_power: None demonstrated in licensed territories; the product is unapproved there and launch pricing is unknown. In China, pricing follows NMPA approval and reimbursement, and Akeso captures it. Any US pricing power will be tested against pembrolizumab-based and durvalumab-based regimens already entrenched as standard of care, and against other PD-1/VEGF bispecifics in development.
competition: Crowded immuno-oncology field: Merck's pembrolizumab, AstraZeneca's durvalumab and bevacizumab, BeiGene's tislelizumab, plus other Chinese PD-1/VEGF bispecifics and standard platinum chemotherapy. HARMONi-2 beat pembrolizumab monotherapy on OS (30.8 vs 22.6 months) and HARMONi-6 beat tislelizumab plus chemotherapy, but these were China-only Akeso-run trials, not global head-to-heads.
team: Led by Executive Chairman and Co-Chief Executive Officer Robert W. Duggan and President and Co-Chief Executive Officer Dr. Maky Zanganeh. Headquartered in Miami, Florida with offices in Palo Alto, Princeton, Dublin and Oxford, about 265 employees, founded 2003. Insiders hold roughly 76.9 percent and institutions about 17.2 percent, with a small 152.3 million share float.
market_strategy: License in a de-risked Chinese bispecific, then fund five Summit-sponsored global Phase III trials and expand into new tumors, adding HARMONi-GU1 bladder in 2026 alongside NSCLC, colorectal and GORTEC's ILLUMINE head and neck study, plus partner combinations with Arcus, Revolution Medicines and GSK. Funding is equity-based through an at-the-market program, including a new 380 million dollar J.P. Morgan facility.
bull: HARMONi-2 OS beat pembrolizumab (30.8 vs 22.6 mo) and HARMONi-6 beat tislelizumab; ESMO 2026 Presidential Symposium selection on 2026-09-22; Jefferies upgraded to Buy 2026-09-09; FDA PDUFA 2026-11-14 is a hard near-term catalyst.
bear: HARMONi primary OS missed significance (HR 0.79, p=0.057); western subgroup HR 0.76 CI 0.52-1.10 crosses one, n=83; single-source Akeso China supply; serial ATM dilution (230.8M Q2, 68.4M after); cash 690.7M vs 147.0M quarterly loss; consensus Hold.
falsifier: A complete response letter on the 2026-11-14 PDUFA for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated NSCLC post-TKI, or a HARMONi-3 squamous-cohort PFS miss in H2 2026.
web_what_changed: Since 2026-06-27: 2026-07-22 updated HARMONi OS HR 0.76 ITT/western; 2026-07-23 Q2 results, cash 690.7M, new 380M ATM with JPM, ridinilazole sale; 2026-08-05 HARMONi-GU1 bladder Phase II/III started; 2026-08-25 Akeso HARMONi-GI1 positive OS in biliary tract; 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-13/15 HARMONi-2 OS statistically significant vs pembrolizumab; 2026-09-22 ESMO 2026 Presidential Symposium selection; 2026-09-09 Jefferies upgrade.
web_not_known_yesterday: not found; no primary disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25. Latest items: 2026-09-22 Business Wire that HARMONi-GI1 will be showcased in an ESMO 2026 Presidential Symposium, and 2026-09-23 reiterations from H.C. Wainwright and UBS. The next hard catalyst is the 2026-11-14 PDUFA date.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Pre-commercial in Summit territories: no product revenue, FY2026 revenue estimate only 3.87M, so growth is clinical-data and trial-enrollment driven, not commercial. Volume means trial patients: over 4,000 dosed in studies globally and over 70,000 commercially in China per Akeso. Neither price nor mix is established in the US, EU or Japan.
web_suppliers: Akeso Inc. (9926.HK) is the sole developer, manufacturer and supplier of ivonescimab drug substance, a single-source China dependency with geopolitical and tariff risk; Summit in-licensed it in January 2023. Combination agents come from partners: enfortumab vedotin (Pfizer/Astellas) for HARMONi-GU1, Arcus casdatifan, Revolution Medicines RAS(ON) inhibitors, GSK risvutatug rezetecan. No disclosed supply constraint.
web_customers: Pre-commercial, so no customer concentration is disclosed. Future customers are oncology treatment centers and payers in North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Japan, where ivonescimab is investigational and unapproved. China commercialization is Akeso's, not Summit's. Summit has no product revenue; company is Miami-based with about 265 employees.
web_who_loses: Merck loses if ivonescimab takes first-line PD-L1-positive NSCLC share from pembrolizumab, as HARMONi-2 suggests, and AstraZeneca loses through durvalumab in biliary tract and bevacizumab in colorectal, plus tislelizumab maker BeiGene and broader PD-1 incumbents in China. Chemotherapy-only comparator arms also become obsolete if the bispecific wins.
web_contradicting_evidence: The HARMONi primary OS analysis missed statistical significance (HR 0.79, p=0.057), the BLA's basis; updated HR 0.76 carries only nominal p=0.0151 and median OS stayed 16.8 vs 14.0 months. Western subgroup HR 0.76 has CI 0.52-1.10 crossing one, n=83. Serious TRAEs 29.9% vs 21.6%. Positive China data are Akeso-run and single-region. Serial ATM dilution: 230.8M in Q2, 68.4M after. Consensus is Hold.
web_if_management_right: FDA approves ivonescimab plus chemotherapy by the 2026-11-14 PDUFA date, launching US EGFR-mutated NSCLC post-TKI, with EU and Japan filings following. HARMONi-3 squamous-cohort PFS events hit in second-half 2026 and are positive, opening first-line NSCLC, then HARMONi-7 versus pembrolizumab, HARMONi-GI3 colorectal and HARMONi-GU1 bladder. Summit re-rates toward the 41 dollar high target and partner Akeso collects milestones and royalties.
web_if_management_wrong: A 2026-11-14 complete response letter over HARMONi's non-significant OS, or a HARMONi-3 squamous miss, removes the near-term US commercial case and pushes the thesis to 2027 non-squamous and HARMONi-7 data. Cash then breaks first: 690.7M at 2026-06-30 against 147.0M non-GAAP quarterly net loss and rising R&D, roughly four to five quarters, forcing more ATM equity or partnering on worse terms.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Akeso Inc. (9926.HK) earns milestones and royalties and gains global validation; Pfizer and Astellas benefit if enfortumab vedotin plus ivonescimab wins HARMONi-GU1; collaborators Revolution Medicines, Arcus Biosciences and GSK gain combination data; contract manufacturers, CROs and trial sites gain volume; EGFR TKI maker AstraZeneca benefits from longer patient survival; PD-L1 testing and diagnostics demand rises.
